info.title: rueder
info.description:
The HTTP interface of a rueder server: the API the web page lives on, under
`/api`, and the Google Reader API for feed reader apps of other makers, under
`/greader`. This description is written from the server's code
(`server/src/openapi.rs` and the `#[utoipa::path]` of each handler), so it
lists every route the server answers, besides the files of the page.

## Logging in

- **The page's API** (`/api`) knows a reader by the session cookie
  `__Host-rueder`, which `POST /api/login` (or a passkey, or OpenID Connect)
  sets. It is `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and `SameSite=Lax`, so it needs HTTPS, or
  `http://localhost` while developing.
- **A request that changes something** (anything but `GET`, `HEAD` and
  `OPTIONS`) is refused with 403 if a browser says it comes from a page of
  another site: by `Sec-Fetch-Site`, or by an `Origin` that is not this
  server. A request without either, such as one from a script, passes this
  check.
- **The Google Reader API** (`/greader`) knows an app by an app password,
  which the reader makes in the page's settings (Settings, Apps).
  `POST /greader/accounts/ClientLogin` takes the account's name and the app
  password as a form and answers with `Auth=<token>`; every other request
  names that token in `Authorization: GoogleLogin auth=<token>`. No cookie
  counts there.

## Answers

- What the page's API sends and takes is JSON, except where an operation says
  otherwise (OPML, the file of an account). The Google Reader API takes forms
  or query parameters, as the apps send them, and answers with JSON or plain
  text.
- **A refusal** has its status and a short plain-text reason, never the
  details of what went wrong inside: 400 for a request the server cannot
  use, 401 without a valid session or app password, 403 for what the account
  may not do, 404 for what is not there or not the account's, 413 for a body
  over the limit (256 KiB, larger only where an operation says so), 429 with
  `Retry-After` (in seconds) over a limit, 500 for a fault of the server.
- **Limits:** every sender and every account has limits on how much it asks
  of the server; logins, lookups of addresses on the internet and what an
  account can make more of (feeds, folders, labels, rules, app passwords)
  have limits of their own.
- **Live updates:** what changes for an account through either API reaches
  its open pages over `GET /api/events` (server-sent events).

## Images

Every image in an article, every thumbnail and icon goes through the server's
image proxy, at addresses the server signs: `/img/...` for the page (with the
session), `/greader/img/...` for an app (signed for its app password).
Addresses are never made by hand; they come in what the API sends.

get.summary: Whether the server and its database answer, for a health check (also `rueder health` on the command line).
The account's events as they happen.
get.description:
A stream of server-sent events, one for each change of the account,
whichever tab, app or fetch made it. An event names what changed; the page
then asks the API for it again. With `Last-Event-ID`, the events since that
one come first, as far as the server still has them; otherwise an event says
to load everything anew.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last event the browser had, to go on from there.

200.description: The events, as `text/event-stream`, until the session ends.

401.description: No valid session: log in first.

429.description: Too many open streams for this account.

post.summary: Logs in with name and password, and with the code of the second factor where the account has one. Answers with who is logged in and sets the session's cookie; a session the browser had before ends.

200.description: Logged in; the answer sets the cookie `__Host-rueder`.

401.description: A wrong name or password (the same answer for both), a wrong code, or `second factor needed`.

403.description: The account is disabled; said only after the right password.

429.description: Too many wrong tries for this name or from this sender; see `Retry-After`.

post.summary: Ends the session of the request, if it has one, and takes the cookie away.

204.description: Logged out; the answer clears the cookie.

get.summary: Who is logged in: the account, what it may do, and what the server offers it.

401.description: No valid session: log in first.

get.summary: What the login page asks before anybody is logged in, to know whether to offer the way through the provider. It says nothing about any account.

post.summary: Starts a login with a passkey, for anybody: the device says whose it is.
post.description:
The answer is what `navigator.credentials.get()` takes; finished with `POST
/api/login/passkey/finish`.

404.description: This server has no passkeys (`PUBLIC_URL` is not set).

429.description: Too many passkey ceremonies open from this sender.

post.summary: Finishes a login with a passkey: the answer of `POST /api/login`, with the session's cookie, and the session counts as one with a second factor.

200.description: Logged in; the answer sets the cookie `__Host-rueder`.

401.description: The passkey is wrong, or belongs to no account here.

404.description: This server has no passkeys (`PUBLIC_URL` is not set).

429.description: Too many wrong tries from this sender; see `Retry-After`.

get.summary: Starts logging in through the OpenID Connect provider: sends the browser there. With `link`, from the logged-in reader's own page, the provider's account is linked to this one instead.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description:
Present to link the provider's account to the one logged in, instead
of logging in.

303.description: On to the provider, or back to the page if linking is refused.

404.description: This server has no OpenID Connect.

get.summary: Where the provider sends the browser back: logs in the account linked to the provider's, or links it, and sends the browser on to the page, which says how it went.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code to exchange for the provider's answer.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The flow it belongs to, as the start gave it.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: What the provider says went wrong, instead of a code.

303.description: Back to the page, logged in, or with what went wrong.

404.description: This server has no OpenID Connect.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
The words. An article is found if it has all of them in its title, its
author, its tags or its text; a word of three letters or more also
finds the words that begin with it.

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: Only in this feed.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description:
Only in the feeds of this folder and the folders inside it. Not
together with `feed`.

delete.summary: Deletes the reader's own account and everything that is its own (see [`accounts::remove`]). Its sessions end, on this device and all others, and so do its connections for live updates, as `events::changed` counts this address as a session that ended. Where the second factor is on, it takes a code as well, as at login: without one the answer is 403 with `second factor needed`, and a wrong one counts like a wrong password. A passkey of the account stands for all of it.

204.description: Deleted; the answer clears the cookie.

401.description: No valid session: log in first.

403.description: Password, code or passkey of the account are wrong.

get.description:
The Digital Asset Links of this site: which Android apps, by package and

200.description: One statement per app, as Android reads them.

404.description: No passkeys on this server, or no app named for them.

Account.description:
An account as an admin sees it.

`GET /api/accounts` answers with a list of them, for admins only.

disabled.description: Disabled by the operator, with `rueder account disable`.

AccountExport.description:
An account as a file, for another rueder. `GET /api/export` answers with
it, and `POST /api/import` reads it.

version.description: The layout of the file, 1. A server reads only the layouts it knows.

settings.description: The settings of the interface, as `GET /api/settings` gives them.

tree.description:
Folders and feeds from the top down, in their order: a folder before
what is in it.

rules.description: The filter rules in their order.

AccountImported.description: What an import did. `POST /api/import` answers with it.

feeds.description: Feeds the account reads now and did not before.

known.description: Feeds of the file the account read already.

articles.description: Articles of the file that were found here.

missing.description:
Articles that were not found: what was read, starred or labelled of
them is lost.

skipped.description:
What the file has that could not be taken: feeds without an address
that can be fetched, articles without an id, labels and rules that
break the rules, rules whose folder or feed is not there.

settings.description: Whether the settings came with it.

AppPassword.description: An app password as the list shows it: never the password itself.

used_at.description: When an app last logged in with it, to the hour; null until one did.

max.description: How many the account can have.

allOf.description: An article opened for reading: the cleaned text of its current version.

oneOf.description: What was different then; null for a change from before rueder noted it.

text_dropped.description:
The retention took its text and left its line in the lists: `html` is
empty, and the original is where `url` points.

hidden_by.description:
The rule that hides the article, if one does: the first of the
account's rules that would, in their order.

Article.description:
An article for reading, with the labels the reader gave it.

`GET /api/feeds/{id}/articles/{seq}` answers with it.

ArticleRef.description: An article, as it can be found on another server.

seq.description:
Its number in its feed on the server the file comes from; with the
feed's number its id in that server's API.

guid.description: Its id in its feed, as the feed gives it.

ArticleVersion.description: One version of an article, cleaned for reading like the current one.

BuildInfo.description:
How this rueder was built and where it runs.

Part of what `GET /api/status` answers, for admins only.

commit.description: The commit it was built from; empty where there was no git directory.

branch.description: The branch that commit was on.

tag.description: The tag on that commit, if it has one.

dirty.description: Something was changed and not committed when this was built.

target.description: The machine it was built for, as `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.

profile.description: `release` or `debug`, and how hard the compiler tried (`3`, `z`, `0`).

ci_run.description: The run of the CI that built it, as an address; empty for a build by hand.

container.description: It runs in a container, as the image of the project does.

Changed.description:
What was different about an article when it last got a new version. A feed
that only rewrites a headline says nothing in the text, and the reader would
look for a change in vain.

ClientReport.description: One error, as the browser saw it.

stack.description:
The lines of the stack in the files of rueder's frontend, as
"_app/immutable/chunks/x.js:12:34", one a line.

browser.description: The browser and its major version, such as "Firefox 140".

ClientReports.description: What `POST /api/reports` reads: at most twenty reports. It answers 204.

ContentReport.description:
A report of a feed or an article.

`POST /api/feeds/{id}/report` and `POST /api/feeds/{id}/articles/{seq}/report`
read it and answer 204.

note.description: What the reader adds, at most 500 characters.

Created.description: The answer to making something: the number it got.

secret.description: In groups of four letters, as it is shown to be typed.

CreatedAppPassword.description: What `POST /api/app-passwords` answers: the app password, this once.

Credentials.description:
What `POST /api/login` reads. It answers with `Me` and sets the session's
cookie. An account with a second factor needs `code` too, from the app or
a recovery code; without it, the answer is 401 with `second factor needed`.

Device.description:
One place a reader is logged in.

`GET /api/sessions` answers with a list of them; `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`
ends one, `DELETE /api/sessions` all but the one that asks.

id.description: A name for the session that is not its token and leads to none.

DropPosition.description:
The side of the node it is dropped on that a node lands on: before it,
after it or, for a folder, inside it.

Durations.description:
How long things took in the hours counted, in milliseconds. The times are null
when nothing was timed.

Enclosure.description: A file that comes with an article, like the episode of a podcast.

type.description: Its media type, such as `audio/mpeg`, if the feed says.

length.description: Its size in bytes, if the feed says.

inline.description: It stood in the article's text and not in the feed's own list.

ExportedAgent.description: Who a feed is fetched as.

ExportedArticle.description: An article the reader did something with.

read.description: Whether it is read, whatever the mark says.

ExportedFeed.description: A subscription, with what the reader did in it.

id.description: The feed's number on the server the file comes from.

url.description: The address of the feed: how it is found again.

own_title.description: The name the reader gave it.

folder.description: The folder it is in, by its path; empty at the top.

last_seq.description: The number of the newest article on the server the file comes from.

oneOf.description:
The article the mark stands at: it and everything before it is read,
but for the articles below that say otherwise. None if the mark is at
the start.

articles.description:
The articles that are read above the mark or unread below it, starred
or labelled.

oneOf.description:
A folder, by its name and the names of the folders it is in, from the
top down.

ExportedNode.description: A folder or a feed of the tree.

ExportedScope.description: Where a rule holds: a folder by its path, a feed by its address.

Farewell.description: What `DELETE /api/account` reads: proof that the reader means it.

password.description: The account's password. An account that has none sends its name.

code.description: A code of the app or a recovery code, where the second factor is on.

oneOf.description: A passkey of the account, instead of all the above.

Feed.description:
A subscription with what the tree shows of its feed.

`folder_id` is the folder it lies in, null at the top.

title.description:
The name the reader gave it, else the feed's own, else, for a feed
that has none (yet), the host of its address.

error.description: Why the last fetch failed, if it did.

fetched.description:
Whether the feed was fetched at all yet. One that came with an OPML
file waits for the next round.

blocked.description:
The operator blocked the feed: nobody sees its articles, and it is not
fetched.

FeedCandidate.description: A feed found at an address.

feed_id.description: The number of the feed if the reader subscribes to it already.

FetchAgent.description:
Who a feed is fetched as: as rueder, or as a browser, for sites that turn
readers like rueder away.

FindFeeds.description:
What `POST /api/feeds/find` reads: the address of a feed or of a page that
names its feeds.

Folder.description: A folder of the tree. `parent_id` is the folder it lies in, null at the top.

moved_to.description:
Where the site sent the request on to, if it did: a site that turns
readers away often sends them to its login.

Email.description: The name of the account (apps call it the e-mail).

Passwd.description: An app password of the account, as Settings, Apps made it.

output.description: `json` for an answer in JSON instead of text.

s.description:
The folder or label to take away: `user/-/label/<name>`. A folder's
feeds move to the top; a label leaves its articles.

a.description: The folder to put it in: `user/-/label/<folder>`.

r.description: The folder to take it out of.

t.description: A name of the reader's own for it.

i.description: The ID of an item; once per item.

a.description:
A state or label to give them: `user/-/state/com.google/read`,
`.../starred` or `user/-/label/<label>`.

r.description: A state or label to take from them.

s.description: The stream to mark read, as for `stream/contents`.

ts.description:
Only what arrived before this time, as `ot` of `stream/contents`, so
that nothing that arrived since the app looked is marked.

quickadd.description: The address of a feed, or of a web page that names one.

dest.description: What it is called from now on: `user/-/label/<name>`.

GreaderUserInfo.description: Who is logged in, as `GET /reader/api/0/user-info` answers.

status.description: Always `ok`: the server answers and its database too.

feeds.description: How many feeds the server knows.

Invite.description:
An invitation as the one who made it sees it. The link itself is shown
once, when it is made.

max_uses.description: For how many accounts it is, and how many it brought.

usable.description: It can still be used: not taken back, not run out, not used up.

Invites.description:
The reader's invitations and how many more they can make.

`GET /api/invites` answers with it.

left.description:
For how many more accounts the reader can make invitations. Left out
for an admin, who has no quota.

days.description: How many days a new invitation is good for.

Label.description: A label. `GET /api/labels` answers with a list of them.

LabelChange.description:
What to change about a label; what is left out stays.

What `PATCH /api/labels/{id}` reads.

LegalLinks.description:
Where the operator's texts are, and which version of the terms counts.

`GET /api/login/ways` answers with it, to anybody.

terms_version.description:
The version of the terms an account has to agree to; none if nobody
has to.

List.description:
A page of a list, the newest article first. For the next page, ask again
with `before` set to the `id` of the last article of this one. A list asked
for with `after` has the oldest article first and goes on the same way,
with `after`.

id.description: Where the article stands in the order of arrival; the anchor for the next page.

updated_at.description: When the current version replaced the one before, if it ever did.

oneOf.description: What was different then; null for a change from before rueder noted it.

ListItem.description: A line of a list, with the labels the reader gave the article.

LoginWays.description:
The ways to log in this server has besides name and password.

`GET /api/login/ways` answers with it, to anybody.

oidc.description: Through the OpenID Connect provider, at `/api/oidc/start`.

registration.description: Anybody can make an account for themselves, at `/api/register`.

legal.description: The operator's legal texts, for the login page to link to.

MadeInvite.description:
A new invitation, with its token, which is never shown again. The link is
the page's address with `?invite=<token>`.

Me.description:
Who is logged in, as the API says it.

`GET /api/me` and `POST /api/login` answer with it.

has_password.description:
Whether the account has a password, which deleting it asks for. One
that logs in only through OpenID Connect has none.

admin_needs_second_factor.description:
An admin whose right waits for a login with a second factor, where the
server wants one of admins.

terms_to_accept.description:
The version of the terms of use the account has yet to agree to, where
the server names one; the page asks before anything else.

content_reports.description: Whether the account may report feeds and articles on this server.

app_api.description:
Whether apps of other makers may log in to this server with app
passwords.

Move.description:
Where a node goes, seen from the node it is dropped on, as in the
interface's own model of the tree.

What `POST /api/tree/move` reads.

NewAccount.description: What `POST /api/accounts` reads, for admins only. It answers with `Created`.

password.description: The first password, which the admin hands over and the reader changes.

NewAppPassword.description:
What `POST /api/app-passwords` reads: a name for it, and the account's
password and, where the second factor is on, one of its codes; or a
passkey instead of both.

uses.description: For how many accounts the link is; one if left out.

NewPasskey.description:
What `POST /api/passkeys/register` reads: a name for the passkey, and what
shows that the owner is there (see [`second_factor::prove`]).

current.description: The password so far. An account that has none needs none.

NewRegistration.description:
What `POST /api/register` reads. It answers with `Me` and sets the
session's cookie, as a login does.

A refusal is 403 with one word: `terms` (the terms of use the server names
were not agreed to), `closed` (no invitation, and registration is not open),
`invite` (the invitation cannot be used), `full` (no room for another
account) or `today` (enough accounts for one day). A name or a
password that cannot be one is 400 with the reason, a name that is taken
409.

accepted_terms.description: The version of the terms of use agreed to, where the server names one.

NodeRef.description: A folder or a subscription, as the tree's changes name them.

OpmlImported.description:
What an import did.

`POST /api/opml` answers with it; the request is the file itself.

feeds.description: Feeds the account reads now and did not before.

known.description: Feeds of the file the account read already.

skipped.description: Outlines that were left out, see [`Outline::skipped`].

Order.description: A new order: every number once, in the order they shall stand in.

Passkey.description: A passkey as the list shows it.

used_at.description: When it last logged in or showed it was the owner; null until then.

PasskeyAnswer.description:
The device's answer to a ceremony that asked for a passkey, which logs in
or shows that the owner is there.

PasskeyChallenge.description:
What a ceremony asks the device: the options for
`navigator.credentials.create()` or `.get()`, in WebAuthn's JSON, with the
name of the ceremony to send the answer back with.

PasskeyRegistration.description:
The device's answer to a ceremony that made a new passkey.

`POST /api/passkeys` reads it.

max.description: How many the account can have.

RecoveryCodes.description:
The recovery codes, shown once.

`POST /api/second-factor/confirm` answers with them.

RegisteredPasskey.description:
What `POST /api/passkeys` answers: the new passkey, and the recovery codes
where it turned the second factor on.

Registering.description:
What the page for registering needs to know before anybody typed a name.

`GET /api/register` answers with it, to anybody; with `?invite=<token>` it
also says whether that invitation can be used.

open.description: Anybody can register, and there is room.

invite.description:
Whether the invitation that was asked about is good: known, not taken
back, not run out, not used up. Left out if none was asked about.

RemovePasskey.description: What `DELETE /api/passkeys/{id}` reads: what shows that the owner is there.

Rename.description:
What `PATCH /api/folders/{id}` and `PATCH /api/feeds/{id}` read. A
subscription without a title of its own goes by its feed's.

ReportKind.description: What kind of error a report is about.

ReportedFeed.description: A feed readers reported, for the status page: its address, never who.

reasons.description: How many reports gave each reason, the most first.

available.description: Whether this server takes reports at all.

ReportsConsentChange.description: What `PUT /api/reports/consent` reads. Off deletes what the account sent.

Rule.description:
A rule as the API takes and gives it.

`GET /api/rules` answers with a list of them. `POST /api/rules`,
`PUT /api/rules/{id}` and `POST /api/rules/preview` read one; there the `id`
counts for nothing, and a rule without `enabled` is enabled.

RuleAction.description: What a rule does with an article it matches.

RuleChanged.description: What a look at the articles changed.

hidden.description: Articles that are hidden now and were not.

shown.description: Articles that were hidden and are back.

RuleField.description: The part of an article a rule looks at.

RuleHits.description: What one of the stored rules finds.

matches.description: The articles the rule matches, whether it is switched on or not,

of.description: of this many it looked at: the newest of each feed in its scope.

RuleMatch.description:
How a rule's pattern is read: as text that stands anywhere, as a whole
word, or as a regular expression.

RuleOutcome.description:
What a change to the rules did to the articles that are there.

`POST /api/rules`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/rules/{id}` answer with it.

RulePreview.description:
How many articles a rule would catch.

What `POST /api/rules/preview` answers.

of.description: of this many it looked at: the newest of each feed in its scope.

RuleScope.description:
Where a rule holds: everywhere, in a folder with all that is in it, or in
one feed.

RulesHits.description:
What `GET /api/rules/hits` answers: for every rule of the account what it
finds among the articles that are there, as a preview of it would say.

SearchHits.description: A page of what a search found, the newest first.

next.description:
Where the next page begins, as `before`; null if nothing older is
left. A page can hold fewer articles than asked for, even none, and
still have a `next`: the server searches for so long per request.

SecondFactor.description:
Whether an account has the second factor, by the app or by passkeys, and
how many recovery codes it has left.

`GET /api/second-factor` answers with it.

on.description: Whether the second factor is on: the app or a passkey.

app.description: Whether the authenticator app is set up.

passkeys.description: How many passkeys the account has.

required_for_admins.description: Whether this server lets admins be admins only with it.

SecondFactorCode.description:
A code from the app.

`POST /api/second-factor/confirm` reads it.

SecondFactorPassword.description:
What setting up reads: the password of the account, which an account that
has none does without, and where the second factor is on already through
passkeys, a recovery code; or a passkey instead of both. Otherwise a
password that got out with a session could add an app of its own.

SecondFactorSetup.description:
A new secret for the app, waiting for a code to confirm it.

`POST /api/second-factor/setup` answers with it.

secret.description: The secret in base32, to type into an app by hand.

uri.description: The `otpauth://` address apps read from the QR code.

qr_svg.description: The QR code of `uri`, as SVG.

SecondFactorSwitchOff.description:
What switching off reads: the password, as for setting up, and a code from
the app or a recovery code; or a passkey instead of both.

build.description: What this build is: commit, branch, when and how it was built.

memory_bytes.description: The memory the server holds, if the system says.

hours.description:
Over how many hours requests, fetches, the feed search, the images and
the problems of the log were counted.

kept_days.description:
How many days the counts are kept for, so the most hours to ask for
are 24 times as many.

hints.description: What looks like a bottleneck or a problem, the most pressing first.

browsers.description: Errors in the browsers of readers who agreed to send them.

reported.description:
Feeds readers reported, with their address: the one place the status
names feeds, as the admins have to look at them. Never who reported.

StateChange.description:
What to change about one article; what is left out stays.

What `PUT /api/feeds/{id}/articles/{seq}/state` reads.

count.description: How often it happened, in all browsers.

versions.description: The versions of the frontend and the browsers it happened in.

StatusBrowserErrors.description: The errors in browsers, for the status page.

available.description: Whether the server takes reports at all.

errors.description: The errors, the one that happened last first. No account is named.

subscribed_feeds.description: Feeds somebody subscribes to, which are the ones fetched.

articles.description: About how many articles: what PostgreSQL estimates.

live_connections.description: Open streams of events: about how many tabs are open.

pool_size.description: The connections of the server: open, idle, at most.

connections.description: All connections to the database, the server's and others'.

cache_hit_ratio.description: The share of blocks found in memory, since the statistics began.

longest_query_s.description: The query that has been running longest, in seconds.

status.description: The status the site answered with, for `status`.

per_hour.description: The most fetches an hour can have at this pace.

running.description: Whether the server fetches feeds at all.

oneOf.description: The pace it fetches at, where it does.

per_hour.description: How many fetches the last hour had, of all kinds.

behind_s.description:
How long the feed that has waited longest past its time has waited, in
seconds; 0 when none is due.

took.description: The fetches of the hours counted.

broken.description: Fetches that failed at the database.

failing.description: Feeds whose last fetch failed, by why.

overdue.description: Feeds fetched more than ten minutes after they were due.

waiting.description: Feeds not fetched yet at all.

StatusFinder.description: The feed search, in the hours counted.

on.description: Whether the server looks at addresses at all.

oneOf.description: Requests to a route take long.
A route failed with errors of the server.
Every connection to the database is in use.
Feeds are fetched later than they are due.

Rounds come full and feeds wait: the pace, not the sites, holds the
fetching back, and `FETCH_ROUND` or `FETCH_EVERY` would let more through.
Many feeds fail.
The fetching does not run.
The database reads much from the disk.
A query has been running for a long time.
The image cache is nearly full.
The server logged errors in the last hour.
Readers were turned away for asking too much.
Browsers reported errors in the last day.
Readers reported feeds that are not blocked.

StatusHint.description: Something on the status page that wants looking at.

failing_sources.description: Sources left alone for now because they failed.

took.description: Images not in the cache, in the hours counted.

target.description: Where in the server it comes from, such as "rueder::fetch".

StatusProblems.description: The warnings and errors of the log.

recent.description: The latest first. The same text from the same place is one.

StatusRequests.description: The requests of the hours counted.

answers.description:
Answers by their first digit: 1xx to 5xx. An image whose source did
not deliver it counts as refused, not as an error of the server; the
image proxy counts it as "source failed".

routes.description: The routes, the slowest first by their 95th percentile.

route.description: The method and the route, such as "GET /api/feeds/{id}/articles".

errors.description: Answers with an error of the server.

bytes.description: With its indexes and, for a table in parts, all of them.

Subscribed.description: The answer to subscribing: the number of the feed.

TermsAgreement.description:
The version of the terms the reader agrees to.

`PUT /api/terms` reads it.

Tree.description:
What `GET /api/tree` answers: the account's folders and subscriptions, each
as a plain list. `parent_id` and `folder_id` say what lies where, `position`
in which order.

hidden.description: How many articles the account's rules hide, for the list of them.

Upto.description:
How far to mark as read: up to a number in the feed, or up to the article
of this `id` in the order of arrival, which is what a mixed list knows.
With `older_than`, only what was published more than that many seconds
ago.

What `POST /api/feeds/{id}/read`, `/api/folders/{id}/read` and `/api/read`
read.

Versions.description:
What `GET /api/feeds/{id}/articles/{seq}/versions` answers: the versions of
the article that are kept, oldest first.

app_password.name: Authorization
app_password.description: GoogleLogin auth=<token>, with the token that POST /greader/accounts/ClientLogin answers for an app password.

session.name: __Host-rueder
session.description: The session, as POST /api/login, a passkey or OpenID Connect set it.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: Logging in and out, with a password, a passkey or OpenID Connect, and who is logged in.

tags.name: Reading
tags.description: The tree of folders and feeds with their unread counts, the lists of articles, an article with its versions, what was read, and the search.

tags.name: Feeds and folders
tags.description: Changing the tree: folders, renaming, moving and ending subscriptions, and the reader's settings.

tags.name: Subscribing
tags.description: Finding the feeds of a web page, subscribing to one, and OPML in and out.

tags.name: Labels
tags.description: The reader's own colored marks for articles.

tags.name: Filter rules
tags.description: Rules that hide articles, or mark them read, as they arrive.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The reader's own account: sessions, password, second factor, passkeys, app passwords, moving it to another rueder, and deleting it.

tags.name: Registration
tags.description: Accounts that make themselves, where the operator allows it, and invitations.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: For admins only: the status of the server and the accounts.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Reports of feeds and articles by their readers, and errors in browsers of readers who agreed to send them.

tags.name: Legal
tags.description: Where the operator's imprint, privacy policy and terms of use are, and agreeing to the terms.

tags.name: Live updates
tags.description: What changes for the account, as server-sent events to every open page.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: The image proxy, at addresses the server signs and sends in what it answers.

tags.name: Android
tags.description: What the Android app needs from the server.

tags.name: Google Reader API
tags.description: For feed reader apps of other makers (NetNewsWire, Read You, Reeder and others), as FreshRSS and Miniflux have it: an app logs in with an app password at `ClientLogin` and names the token it gets in `Authorization: GoogleLogin auth=<token>`. Requests are forms or query parameters; what only reads takes GET and POST alike, as some apps send everything as a form.
